key_fields.sql: select z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone, count(t.pulocationid) as cash_trips from ops.zones z left join lake.trips t on t.pulocationid = z.locationid and t.payment_type = 2 group by z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone order by z.locationid
key_fields.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

value.sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COALESCE(agg.cnt, 0) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT PULocationID, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM lake.trips
    WHERE payment_type = 2
    GROUP BY PULocationID
) agg ON agg.PULocationID = z.LocationID
ORDER BY z.LocationID;
value.change_summary: Pre-aggregate trips by PULocationID after filtering payment_type=2, then join the tiny aggregated result to zones, avoiding a large hash join and group-by on the full trip set.
value.risk_notes: None; the rewrite preserves all zones rows and produces identical counts because the subquery groups by the exact join key before the left join.
